newsitem.title: FRANCE: Ariane to launch Italian defence satellite.
newsitem.headline: Ariane to launch Italian defence satellite.

text.p: Western Europe's heavy satellite launch company Arianespace has won a contract to launch a satellite for Italy's Ministry of Defence, the company said on Wednesday.

It said a new generation Ariane-5 rocket would launch the 2.5-tonne SICRAL telecommunications satellite from the European Space Agency's (ESA) launch centre in French Guiana on the northeast coast of South America in late 1999.
It was Arianespace's first commercial contract specifically assigning an Ariane-5 rocket for a specific satellite launch.

Arianespace said SICRAL will be an integrated satellite communications system to provide secure telecommunications for the Italian Ministry of Defence and civil security forces for both domestic needs and remote operations.

"SICRAL features highly innovative technology, making it the benchmark for the 21st century defence satcom systems. This cutting edge technology will also make the Italian space industry a highly competitive player in the international marketplace," it said.

The satellite will be built by the SITAB consortium led by Italy's BPD Difesa e Spazio (Fiat Avio Group) and Alenia Spazio. The ground control centre will be built by Nuova Telespazio. Its cost was not disclosed.

The first Ariane-5 rocket exploded shortly after its maiden launch on June 4 in a major setback for the $8 billion dollar Ariane-5 programme aimed at keeping Western Europe's lead in launching heavy satellites well into the next century.
The failure caused Arianespace to postpone the second Ariane-5 launch from September to next April at the earliest, and delay the scheduled commercial debut of Ariane-5 for at least a year from 1997.

Arianespace president Charles Bigot announced last month that his company will make additional order for at least five more flight-proven Ariane-4 rockets -- a rocket that has failed only three times in 62 launches.
Industry analysts said SICRAL would be launched aboard an Ariane-4 if the Ariane-5 programme encountered further delays.
The Paris-based Arianespace company said it has firm orders to launch 43 heavy satellites worth an estimated $3.4 billion.
